 TL has several structural divisions within it which signal shifts in both the plot and point
of view. The poem is divided into four sections: the induction, which includes the narra-
tor’s description of the landscape at sunrise, and sees the narrator fall into a visionary state
(ll. 1–40), the beginning of the vision and the description of the triumphal procession of
‘Life’ (ll. 41–179), the conversation between the narrator and Rousseau about those in and
around the procession (ll. 180–308), and Rousseau’s tale of his vision and encounter with
the shape all light (ll. 308–546). All the transitions between these sections are marked by
